body:
GREG, 2026-11-11 about 07:06Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant (mailbox 43498a6e #921, message c4fba59a), verbatim: „No to nie robmy takich designów. To są cięzkie limity, nie sprawdzaja sie u nas. Limity resetujace operacje powinny byc minuta. A logowac ostrzeżenie po 10 sekunach. Inaczej znowu system przestaje działać!!!”
Context: TermAl's 6000 ms host-adapter deadline killed every `engram work evaluate` submission into TermAl's store (w-ccc13083eaac).
Decision, per Asistant's scope note:
- Any limit that aborts or resets an operation is 60 s.
- At 10 s, log a warning without interrupting.
- First target: TermAl's Engram evaluate adapter. Then review similar hard limits in both projects, and file or fix the fitting places.
- Keep idempotency, and don't duplicate unknown outcomes.
- The write-performance diagnosis continues.
- Ship as fast as possible, confirmed by a test and by an actual same-key resubmit of the retained evaluations, without asking Greg again.

ARCHITECTURAL INTERPRETATION (Kimi::Consultant, 2026-11-11; coordinated with Engram::Fable and Termal::Fable2):
- Every abort/reset limit shorter than 60 s becomes 60 s; existing longer bounds are not shortened. At 10 s emit one bounded warning with the operation/workRef/attempt id and elapsed time, without interrupting and without including a full source_id. The hard bound still contains a genuine hang and capacity loss; it is not a performance fix.
- Timeout means UNKNOWN, not write_failed and not proof that no commit happened. never_started remains a distinct outcome. A lock retry keeps the same absolute deadline rather than resetting it.
- Before retrying, read the actual record. Only an explicitly idempotent operation may be replayed, with the same key and verdicts. If the record exists, consume it; if it is absent, replay that operation. An unknown outcome never duplicates work and never justifies restarting the whole item. This does not replace w-ccc13083eaac's write-performance diagnosis and adds no new gate.
